name: Gypsum Application Rate Calculator
seoTitle: Gypsum Application Rate Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Gypsum (calcium sulfate) adds calcium without raising pH, and it improves the structure of sodic clay soils. Free gypsum application rate calculator: enter yo
summary:
Gypsum (calcium sulfate) adds calcium without raising pH, and it improves the structure of sodic clay soils. It returns gypsum rate, gypsum needed and 25 kg bags, and the panel shows all of them at once.

The rate depends on the soil's exchangeable sodium and its clay content — typically 0.5–2 tonnes per acre, or 1–5 tonnes per hectare. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Gypsum Application Rate
sections.html:
Gypsum (t/ha) = texture factor × (ESP − target ESP) ÷ 10, where the texture factor is 1.5 for sand, 3 for loam and 5 for clay

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
ESPexchangeable sodium percentage, the share of cation sites holding sodium%
gypsumcalcium sulfate dihydrate, CaSO₄·2H₂O—
t/hatonnes per hectaret/ha

sections.title: How do I use the Gypsum Application Rate?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the area and the soil texture.
  2. Enter the exchangeable sodium percentage from a soil test and the level you are aiming for.
  3. Read the rate in tonnes per hectare, the total and the number of bags.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: area of 1 ha, soil texture set to 3.0, exchangeable sodium percentage of 15%, target esp of 5%.

Substituting them into the formula gives gypsum rate of 3 t/ha, gypsum needed of 3 t, 25 kg bags of 120.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
under 1 t/haLighta maintenance application on a slightly sodic soil
1 – 3 t/haStandardthe usual correction for a loam at 15% ESP
over 5 t/haHeavysplit across two seasons and follow with leaching water

  • Gypsum supplies calcium and sulfur but does not change pH. If the soil is also acid, lime is the amendment you want, not gypsum.

  • Gypsum works by exchanging calcium for sodium on the clay, and the displaced sodium then needs water to leach away. Without drainage and leaching, the sodium stays.

  • It is also the standard cure for clay dispersion and for subsoil acidity at depth, where lime cannot be incorporated.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Applying gypsum to raise pH — it does not, and the mistake costs a season.
  • Spreading the full rate in one pass on a heavy clay with no drainage.
  • Ignoring the sodium: gypsum on a non-sodic soil does little for structure.

faq.a: 1–3 t/ha for a loam at 15% ESP; up to 5 t/ha for a sodic clay.
No. It is pH-neutral; use elemental sulfur or aluminium sulfate to acidify.

faq.q: Can I apply gypsum with fertiliser?
faq.a: Yes, but not mixed with ammonium sulfate or superphosphate in the same hopper.

faq.q: What does the Gypsum Application Rate actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns gypsum rate, gypsum needed and 25 kg bags. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
